ccasion occurs in cell DTX/DRX active time so that the most recent, no later than the CSI reference resource, occasion of CSI-IM and/or NZP CSI-RS associated with the CSI resource setting is available. Thus, when the UE is configured with LowBandCA-Switching, the most recent CSI measurement occasion of semi-persistent CSI-RS resource or periodic CSI-RS resource on the serving cell should be defined and should occur in valid time of the serving cell for CSI report configured by CSI-ReportConfig. For periodic CSI-RS and semi-persistent CSI-RS on a serving cell configured in CSI report configuration in CSI-ReportConfig, The most recent CSI measurement occasion of semi-persistent CSI-RS resource or periodic CSI-RS resource on the serving cell occurs in the symbols available for CSI-RS receptions as described in Clause 24 of TS 38.213. The related TP to TS 38.214 is given in appendix TP#1. In addition, in the previous meeting, some companies proposed to change a valid downlink slot as a slot not overlapping with any slot assigned to the other serving cell. Note that the valid downlink slot is part of the definition of CSI reference resource. CSI reference resource is a virtual resource, it is used to define a timeline so that UE can have enough time to calculate the CSI and prepare the reporting, as well as to define some assumptions for the CSI calculation. It is meaningless to change the definition of CSI reference resource to change a valid downlink slot as a slot not overlapping with any slot assigned to the other serving cell. As shown in above Figure 4, it can’t address the issue that the occasion defined by the current specification to be used for CSI calculation may be unavailable as mentioned above. Specification impact due to RAN4’s LS In the previous meeting, RAN4 sent a LS to RAN1 with the following information [4]. According to the LS from RAN4 that for the SCell which is in activation procedure, the RRC configured switching pattern for SDL SCell is applied. Note that a UE can always be provided with a switching pattern, but the application of the RRC configured switching pattern is specified in RAN4’s specification. So, the current description in RAN1 specification is not correct. Endorse TP#2 to TS 38.213 for alignment. Conclusions In this contribution, we express our views from both theoretical and practical perspectives and provide our proposal accordingly. The observations and the proposals are listed as follows. Observation 1: In addition to the antenna element placement affecting the polarization direction, the polarization direction also depends on the wire length connecting antenna element and oscillator. Observation 2: The maximum wire-length difference between antenna elements connecting to oscillator can exceed half a wavelength, and the polarization orientations of antennas at different locations vary substantially, showing fully randomized behavior across the measured frequency bands. Observation 3: UE implementation method is diverse among different vendors or companies, it would not be practical to use one model to cover different implementation specific variations. Proposal 1: To enhance the handheld antenna model, the parameters particularly related to polarization orientation should follow the actual measurement results of the real terminal products. Proposal 2: The polarization orientation issue in channel model should be addressed based on enough measurement results on the actual terminal product. Proposal 3: For periodic CSI-RS and semi-persistent CSI-RS on a serving cell configured in CSI report configuration in CSI-ReportConfig, The most recent CSI measurement occasion of semi-persistent CSI-RS resource or periodic CSI-RS resource on the serving cell occurs in the symbols available for

I-RS, no later than the CSI reference resource, (defined in [4, TS 38.211]) associated with the CSI resource setting. If the higher layer parameter timeRestrictionForChannelMeasurements in CSI-ReportConfig is set to "Configured", the UE shall derive the channel measurements for computing L1-RSRP reported in uplink slot n based on only the most recent, no later than the CSI reference resource, occasion of SS/PBCH or NZP CSI-RS (defined in [4, TS 38.211]) associated with the CSI resource setting. If the transmission of a first SS/PBCH blocks is indicated and the transmission of a second SS/PBCH blocks is activated [6, TS 38.213], the UE shall derive the channel measurements for computing L1-RSRP reported in uplink slot n based on only the most recent, no later than the CSI reference resource, occasion of the first SS/PBCH and/or the second SS/PBCH associated with the CSI resource setting. <Unrelated part omitted> --------------------------------------- End of the TP for TS 38.214--------------------------------------------- SSB EPRE and CSI-RS EPRE As specified in TS 38.214, the downlink SS/PBCH SSS EPRE can be derived from the SS/PBCH downlink transmit power given by the parameter ss-PBCH-BlockPower provided by higher layers, and the downlink CSI-RS EPRE can be derived from the SS/PBCH block downlink transmit power given by the RRC parameter ss-PBCH-BlockPower and CSI-RS power offset given by the RRC parameter powerControlOffsetSS. In Case#1 where only on-demand SSB is transmitted, the UE is provided with od-ss-PBCH-BlockPower rather than ss-PBCH-BlockPower. Therefore, when the on-demand SSB is activated, the downlink SS/PBCH SSS EPRE should be derived from the OD-SSB downlink transmit power which is given by the RRC parameter od-ss-PBCH-BlockPower, and the downlink CSI-RS EPRE is derived from this value and the CSI-RS power offset. Proposal 3: In case#1, when on-demand SSB is activated, The downlink SS/PBCH SSS EPRE is derived from the on-demand SSB downlink transmit power given by the RRC parameter od-ss-PBCH-BlockPower. The downlink CSI-RS EPRE is derived from the on-demand SSB downlink transmit power given by the RRC parameter od-ss-PBCH-BlockPower and CSI-RS power offset given by the RRC parameter powerControlOffsetSS. Adopt the following TP for clause 4.1 of TS 38.214. --------------------------------------- Start of the TP for TS 38.214-------------------------------------------

Based on discussion in RAN1, following conclusion is reached: The power headroom is calculated without applying the MIMO scale factor s from section 7 of 38.213, since both the UE and the network are aware of the scaling factor s, they should use it to adjust the power headroom to determine the power actually transmitted by the UE. ich we present in this contribution. In RAN1#108-e [2], RAN1 made the following agreement related to TCI state indication for CORESET#0. A remaining open point is how to determine the QCL assumptions for DL channels and spatial relation for UL channels associated with a CORESET with index 0 after a random access procedure not initiated by PDCCH order that triggers a contention-free random access procedure. In Rel-15/16, the quasi-co-location/TCI state of the CORESET with index 0 is described in clause 10.1 of TS 38.213. In Rel-15/16 [TS 38.213]: A similar principle can be used for a CORESET with index 0 when configured to follow the unified TCI state (or not configured to not follow the unified TCI state): the TCI state/quasi-co-location is determined by the indicated (unified) TCI state, or the most recent random access procedure if no unified TCI state has been indicated after the most recent random access procedure. Proposal 1: When CORESET 0 has been configured by RRC to follow the unified TCI state (or not configured to no follow the unified TCI state), the TCI state/quasi-co-location is determined by the indicated (unified) TCI state, or the most recent random access procedure if no unified TCI state has been indicated after the most recent random access procedure.  scheduling. In our view, difference between DCI for TCI state update and for SCell dormancy would stem only from the indicated functionality. Therefore, it would be a bit strange for us if RAN1 would take another direction for SCell dormancy indicating DCI from TCI state update DCI. One could indeed argue that such restriction on SLIV allowed for DCI for particular use cases may cause inflexible configurations. However, again, whether/how significant such inflexibility would be not very clear. Moreover, considering the agreement above, we think just to take an unified direction for similar functionalities would be implementation friendly. Given the above consideration, our view is as follows: Proposal 2: Adopt TP#1 for TS 38.213 for DCI format indicating SCell dormancy without scheduling PDSCH reception Reason for change: UE behavior for receiving SCell dormancy indication via DCI 1_1 when multi-PDSCH scheduling is configured is not clear Summary of change: Clarify that DCI format 1_1 including SCell dormancy indication indicates a TDRA row with only one SLIV entry Consequence if not approved: SCell dormancy may not work in FR2-2
